To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) the ISDM was not a single, coherent, and integrated entity; (2) it was a bundle of interrelated and interdependent knowledge; (3) it was not an immutable entity; (4) its components were not static and fixed; and (5) its components were subject to adaptation, change, and reconfiguration.
the ISDM was diffused and infused through the process of “contextualization.”
the diffusion and infusion of ISDMs are shaped by the structure and culture, and by the social, technical, and organizational context of organizations.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the development of an information system is shaped by the context in which it is deployed.
the diffusion and infusion of IS knowledge in the form of a de-contextualised ISDM.
the diffusion of ISDMs, which are knowledge bundles, and how these bundles become infused within the organizational context.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
this study has shown how an ISDM, in this case the SSADM, is a “bundle of knowledge” that is deployed in an organizational context and is then adapted and infused into the organization’s practices.
the ISDM is not the only factor that determines the success of an IS project; the structure and culture, as well as the people involved, are also key factors.
the ISDM is not a static and unchanging entity but rather a dynamic and adaptive process.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ISDM was not used as a prescriptive method, and the project was a hybrid, with a number of different approaches and methods being used.
the process of diffusion and infusion is a complex and multi-faceted process.
organizations are not passive recipients of ISDMs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
organizations adapt and deploy ISDMs to suit their needs and that the knowledge contained within the method is diffused throughout the organization through the process contextualization.
the process of knowledge diffusion and infusion is a complex process, which involves the interaction between the knowledge bundle, the organizational structure and culture, and the social context.

the process of contextualizing knowledge bundles is an essential part of the knowledge diffusion process and is not a one-off activity, but an ongoing process that is subject to continual change and adaptation as the context evolves.
